name: Gradient-driven Sampling
definition: A sampling strategy that refines step sizes according to the magnitude of the scalar field gradient, which indicates local feature sharpness; smaller steps are taken near high-gradient regions resembling surfaces to capture transitions accurately.
summary: Gradient-driven Sampling is a dynamic step size adjustment technique that adapts ray marching traversal to local gradient magnitude, balancing accuracy and cost by taking smaller steps in high-gradient regions and larger steps in smooth interiors.
